summary: This bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to make any noncitizen convicted of a felony or two misdemeanors deportable.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends immigration law to expand deportability grounds for criminal convictions. It contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget authority. Any indirect enforcement costs are speculative and not addressed in the text.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
The bill does not regulate firearms, background checks, or gun ownership rights.

Section 2 explicitly expands the criminal grounds for deportability under the Immigration and Nationality Act by making any alien convicted of a felony or two misdemeanors removable. This directly strengthens enforcement and removal mechanisms, aligning with policies that restrict immigration through stricter border and interior enforcement.
No provisions relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill contains no defense or military spending authorizations.
No environmental or regulatory provisions are present.
The legislation does not modify welfare programs, eligibility, or benefits.
No education funding, policy, or school-related provisions exist.
While felonies and misdemeanors could include drug offenses, the bill addresses only the immigration consequences of such convictions rather than drug enforcement or decriminalization policy itself.
The bill imposes immigration consequences for criminal convictions but does not alter sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal procedure in the justice system.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization measures are included.
The bill has no fiscal or debt-related provisions.
No provisions address LGBTQ legal protections or rights.
The bill does not authorize, modify, or affect foreign assistance programs.
No election administration, voting access, or election integrity measures are present.
The legislation contains no technology regulation or privacy provisions.
No labor, union, or employment law changes are made.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or civil rights protections.
